raw_case_text:
A 38-year-old male patient, diagnosed with retroviral infection and disseminated tuberculosis presented with weakness and numbness of the right hand of 2 weeks duration. He also noticed an edematous reddish raised lesion on the inner aspect of right hand, which he attributed to the topical agent he used for relieving the numbness. Pain was present on the right elbow and forearm. The patient had been on antitubercular therapy (ATT) followed by antiretroviral therapy (ART), 5 months prior to presentation at our department. The CD4 count was 67 cells/muL during initiation of HAART.
Dermatological examination showed a single well-defined erythematous plaque, 20 x 5 cm with raised borders on the ulnar aspect of right hand and distal forearm, extending to the palm [Figures 1 and 2]. A satellite lesion was present on the upper part of forearm, which also showed erythema and edema. All modalities of sensations were lost in these lesions. Both ulnar nerves were thickened with tenderness on the right side. Slit skin smears from the earlobe, lesional, and normal skin were negative. Histopathological examination showed dermal edema, diffuse granulomas composed of Langhans type giant cells, surrounded by epithelioid cells, lymphocytes, multinucleated giant cells, and fibroblasts with perivascular lymphocytic infiltrate, consistent with Hansen's disease borderline tuberculoid type, with features suggesting type 1 lepra reaction [Figures 3-6]. AFB stain was negative. CD4 count after 5 months showed a rise to 160 cells/muL. The viral RNA load was not measured due to lack of facilities.
Thus correlating the clinical, bacteriological, and histopathological features, a diagnosis of Hansen's disease borderline tuberculoid with type 1 lepra reaction presenting as IRIS was made. MB-MDT was started, avoiding rifampicin from the regimen, as patient was also on ATT. HAART was continued and systemic steroids were also given in tapering doses. On follow up there was marked alleviation of his symptoms. However, the patient succumbed within 3 months to a brain tuberculoma.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 38-year-old male presenting with weakness and numbness of the right hand for two weeks, accompanied by a painful raised skin lesion on the forearm.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient presented with a 2-week history of acute weakness and numbness involving the right hand, associated with right forearm and elbow pain. Concurrently, he noted an edematous reddish raised plaque on the inner aspect of the right hand and distal forearm, which he had treated with an over-the-counter liniment without relief. Five months prior to presentation, he had commenced antitubercular therapy followed by antiretroviral therapy.
subjective.past_medical_history: Retroviral (HIV) infection with severe immunosuppression (nadir CD4 count 67 cells/muL) and disseminated tuberculosis, receiving antitubercular therapy (ATT) and highly active antiretroviral therapy (HAART) for 5 months prior to presentation.
subjective.review_of_systems: Numbness and weakness of the right hand, right upper extremity pain, and skin lesions; denies constitutional symptoms or prior neurological deficits.

objective.physical_examination: Dermatologic: Single well-defined erythematous plaque measuring 20 x 5 cm with raised borders on the ulnar aspect of the right hand and distal forearm extending into the palm, with an edematous erythematous satellite plaque on the upper forearm. Neurologic/Sensory: Complete loss of all sensory modalities over the plaque and satellite lesion; motor weakness in the right hand. Peripheral nerves: Bilateral ulnar nerve thickening with marked tenderness over the right ulnar nerve.
objective.routine_investigations: Slit skin smears from earlobes, lesional skin, and normal skin: Negative for acid-fast bacilli.
objective.advanced_workup: Skin biopsy of forearm lesion: Dermal edema with diffuse epithelioid cell granulomas containing Langhans multinucleated giant cells, surrounding lymphocytes, fibroblasts, and perivascular lymphocytic infiltrate; tissue acid-fast stain (AFB) was negative.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation:
Definitive diagnosis: Immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome (IRIS) manifesting as unmasked Hansen's disease (borderline tuberculoid type) with Type 1 lepra reaction (reversal reaction) and acute ulnar neuritis in an HIV-infected patient following immune recovery on HAART and ATT (CD4 count increased from 67 to 160 cells/muL), confirmed by histopathology; complicated by fatal cerebral tuberculoma.
Plan & Outcome: Treated with multibacillary multidrug therapy (MB-MDT) modified to omit rifampicin (as rifampicin was already included in his concurrent ATT regimen), continuation of HAART, and tapering doses of systemic corticosteroids for Type 1 reaction. Cutaneous and neurological symptoms alleviated significantly; however, the patient succumbed within three months to a central nervous system tuberculoma.
